rv.q: So the core of the comedy is dampened a tad in moments when it departs from the humor, to level a dose of somewhat heavy handed preachiness.
A stellar cast more than makes up for some of the inherent unevenness in Charles Busch’s The Tale of the Allergist’s Wife, produced at Skokie Theatre as part of MadKap Productions’s 2023-24 season.
Although this play once opened to critical acclaim, it nevertheless feels much too anachronistic and dated.

cn.t: This Jewish domestic comedy delivers laugh-out-loud moments and top-notch production values, though the 2001 script feels dated and could use updating for modern audiences.
